Watched Peddi and came out more frustrated than disappointed because this felt like a movie with huge potential that never decided what it wanted to be.

My biggest issue was the lack of focus. In a 3-hour film, why try to fit 3 different sports and make the hero succeed across multiple levels? Instead of creating one strong sports journey and making us emotionally invest in it, the movie kept adding new tracks and diluted the impact.

Ram Charan is shown doing everything—making jaggery, playing cricket, wrestling, running despite injury, winning medals—and after a point it stopped feeling inspiring and started feeling overloaded. A great sports drama makes you root for one difficult journey. Here it felt like the screenplay kept changing lanes before anything fully landed.

What disappointed me most is that Ram Charan clearly put in tremendous effort. You can see the commitment in the physical performance, fights and dance sequences. But effort alone cannot replace strong writing. Many dances were edited or choreographed so fast that the moments didn’t stay with you.

The action portions also felt weak. Usually mass movies build hero elevation through memorable payoff moments, but here the fights felt repetitive and surprisingly ordinary. The hero struggled through long fight sequences but the movie never converted that struggle into emotionally satisfying moments.

Jagapathi Babu’s character felt underused too. He has the screen presence to carry emotional weight, but here the role felt reduced and never created the impact it could have.

Janhvi Kapoor’s character and political angle also felt disconnected. Her father’s election setup looked important initially, but by the climax the conflict and alliances didn’t feel emotionally earned. The love story itself barely felt developed. There wasn’t enough chemistry or progression between the lead pair to make it memorable.

The heroine’s presentation also didn’t work for me—not because of the actor, but because of the writing and visual treatment. Instead of building authenticity and depth into the character, the movie seemed more interested in adding glamour where it wasn’t necessary.

Another thing I couldn’t understand: why have separate conflicts and villains around different sports? One track for cricket, another for wrestling, politics somewhere else, romance somewhere else. Why not choose one sport, one central conflict and one strong antagonist? It would have made the story tighter and easier to connect with.

Too many characters entered and exited without purpose. Supporting roles didn’t leave much impression and even some simple dialogues didn’t feel natural or easy to connect with.

For me, Peddi tried to be a sports drama, village drama, political drama, romance, mass entertainer and action film all at once—and ended up not excelling in any one of them.

This felt less like a complete movie and more like a collection of ideas competing with each other.
